# Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost

> Exact integrated-force costs and attainable sensitivity tradeoffs for
> static-detuning robustness of two-qubit gates mediated by one ideal oscillator.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost
Author: Ruge Lin
Contact: [gogoko699@gmail.com](mailto:gogoko699@gmail.com)

This repository is a research record and a guide for the author's self-directed
learning. This index describes its scope and points to the current scientific
account; it is not a substitute for the assumptions and proofs in those files.

## Questions addressed

- When does first-order detuning robustness require additional integrated force?
- Which finite control spaces make angle robustness free, costly, or infeasible?
- What is the smallest angle sensitivity attainable at a fixed force budget?
- How do displacement robustness and angle robustness differ?
- What is the exact cost of quartic-or-better small-detuning thermal infidelity?
- Why can a narrow positive-frequency force band produce unbounded cost ratios?
- How does independent-pulse stabilization lead to an exact joint optimization?

Relevant terminology: oscillator-mediated entangling gates; spin-dependent
forces; geometric phase; trapped-ion pulse design; static number detuning;
trajectory overlap; force-space projection; conjugate quadratures; spectral
optimization; equality S-lemma; joint numerical range.

- [Self-contained theory](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost/blob/main/research/THEORY.md): dynamics, matrix reduction, exact costs, attaining controls, and thermal-channel consequences.
- [Exact sensitivity frontier](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost/blob/main/research/SENSITIVITY_FRONTIER.md): the optimum at every feasible budget, endpoint cases, and a worked two-tone example.

- [Control examples](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost/blob/main/research/CONTROL_EXAMPLES.md): a symmetric four-tone space, a fixed-first-pulse comparison, and the distinction between integrated cost and individual peak caps.

## Single learning anchor and attribution

The selected learning anchor is R. Blümel et al., *Power-optimal, stabilized
entangling gate between trapped-ion qubits* (2021),
[arXiv:1905.09292v2, including its supplement](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.09292v2).
It is a research article with detailed derivations. Its main text develops
projected spectral pulse optimization; supplement S16 treats independently
stabilized pulses. The tutorial bridge explains the change of control class
and normalization before comparing the optimization tasks.

- [Matched related work and source passages](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Oscillator-Gate-Robustness-Cost/blob/main/research/RELATED_WORK.md): inherited ingredients, exact source locations, and the scoped joint optimum.

Independent-pulse stabilization, quadrature gates, displacement moments,
trajectory-overlap sensitivity, and the leading thermal fidelity expansion
have direct predecessors. Equality-S-lemma and numerical-range arguments are
established mathematics. The repository's contribution is the exact jointly
attained force-resource classification and sensitivity frontier in its stated
model, with spectral and full-gate consequences.

## Scope needed when using the results

- One ideal linear oscillator mediates two independently chosen complex forces
  in the same prescribed finite-dimensional, nominally closed force space.
- The error is an unknown static number detuning. Controls do not depend on it.
- Comparisons fix the duration, force normalization, control space, and nonzero
  unwrapped target angle in exp(i Theta_0 Z_1 Z_2).
- Cost is E = integral (|f_1|^2 + |f_2|^2) dt, the integrated squared effective
  force. It is not automatically laboratory input power or a peak-amplitude cost.
- With phase matrix K and positive overlap matrix D, the nominal cost is
  |Theta_0| / ||K|| and the angle-robust cost is
  |Theta_0| / min_{zeta real} ||K - zeta D||. A zero denominator means infeasibility.
- Nominal closure, first-order displacement robustness, first-order angle
  robustness, and phase evenness are different requirements.
- Quartic-or-better thermal infidelity additionally needs both first force
  moments to vanish. The oscillator initially has an uncorrelated thermal state
  with fixed finite mean occupation; the statements are local in detuning.
- Angle robustness has no additional cost when the space remaining after
  displacement constraints is conjugation invariant. Imposing displacement
  constraints can itself cost.
- The positive-band penalty compares matched optima within each force space;
  the nominal cost also grows along the four-tone family.
